s1.syndrome_frame: Impacted tooth with associated radiographic lesion
salient_findings: Radiopaque lesion in the left mandibular anterior region
key_facts: 22-year-old woman
All permanent teeth erupted except third molars and lower left lateral incisor
Mild spacing between lower left central incisor and canine
Class II, Division 1 malocclusion
Crowding in maxillary anterior region
No history of prior dental extractions
Unerupted lower left lateral incisor with associated radiopaque lesion
Radiopaque lesion surrounded by thin radiolucent halo
Lesion obstructs eruption path of tooth

shortlist.label: Compound odontoma
shortlist.why_kept: Radiopaque lesion associated with unerupted tooth

shortlist.label: Dentigerous cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Common cause of tooth impaction with radiographic lesion

shortlist.label: Adenomatoid odontogenic tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Known to cause tooth impaction and has radiographic appearance similar to the case

shortlist.label: Complex odontoma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to compound odontoma, can cause tooth impaction and has radiographic lesion

shortlist.label: Odontogenic keratocyst
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause tooth impaction and has radiographic appearance similar to the case

raw.rationale: The radiopaque lesion associated with the unerupted lower left lateral incisor, surrounded by a thin radiolucent halo, is consistent with the characteristics of a compound odontoma, which is a type of odontogenic tumor that can obstruct tooth eruption.

rejected.label: Dentigerous cyst
rejected.why: Dentigerous cysts are typically associated with an unerupted tooth but are characterized by a radiolucency surrounding the crown of the tooth, not a radiopaque lesion.

rejected.label: Adenomatoid odontogenic tumor
rejected.why: Adenomatoid odontogenic tumors can be associated with unerupted teeth but are more commonly seen in the anterior maxilla and have a distinct histological appearance.

rejected.label: Complex odontoma
rejected.why: Complex odontomas are a type of odontogenic tumor but are less likely to be associated with a single unerupted tooth and have a more complex radiographic appearance.

rejected.label: Odontogenic keratocyst
rejected.why: Odontogenic keratocysts are characterized by a radiolucency with scalloped borders and are not typically associated with a radiopaque lesion.
